reason: council-remediation-2026-07-20/agent-O-utilities: arithmetic error in correct_option_id. Largest waste stream is biodegradable at 60% (200 kg/day x 0.60 = 120 kg/day), non-recyclable is only 25% (50 kg/day). Original correct_option_id c (3,600 L) was mathematically inconsistent with the stem; correct answer is b (1,440 L). Recomputation shown in rationale.

checked_sources.label: RA 9003 Ecological Solid Waste Management Act

source_audit_support.citation: RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000) Section 3, Segregation of Solid Waste; bulk density 0.4 m3/100 kg per stem.

proposed.text: A 150-unit condominium generates 200 kg/day solid waste and plans segregation per RA 9003 with storage for 3 days. If biodegradable waste is 60%, non-recyclable 25%, recyclable 10%, and hazardous 5%, calculate the storage volume needed for the largest waste stream (assume 0.4 m3/100 kg bulk density).
proposed.rationale: Largest stream = biodegradable at 60%. Daily biodegradable mass = 200 kg/day x 0.60 = 120 kg/day. 3-day storage = 120 x 3 = 360 kg. Bulk density conversion: 0.4 m3 per 100 kg = 4 L/kg. Volume = 360 kg x 4 L/kg = 1,440 L = 1.44 m3. Correct answer is b (1,440 L). The previously marked answer c (3,600 L) would require 900 kg of biodegradable waste stored, which corresponds to 4.5 days of the full 200 kg/day stream (not the biodegradable fraction) - an arithmetic error. Option a (720 L) would correspond to 180 kg (non-recyclable stream 25% x 200 x 3 = 150 kg x 4 L/kg = 600 L, not 720 L). Option d (7,200 L) corresponds to total unsegregated waste for 3 days plus a factor-of-5 error.
proposed.explanation: The largest waste stream by mass is biodegradable (60%). Per RA 9003 Section 3, segregated biodegradable storage must be sized for the daily generation times the storage interval. Volume = (200 kg/day x 0.60) x 3 days x (0.4 m3/100 kg) = 1.44 m3 = 1,440 L.
